extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and stakeholders (including environmental law practitioners and parties) who may wish to submit comments on the lodged consent decree
extracted.subtask_short: commenting on DOJ consent decree notice
extracted.subtask_description: Submitting public comments in response to a Department of Justice Federal Register notice lodging a proposed consent decree (here, under CERCLA and the Clean Water Act). Includes requirements on timing, addressing and referencing comments, submission methods, public filing risks, and where to access the proposed decree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments must be submitted no later than thirty (30) days after the publication of this notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publication of this notice opens a period for public comment on the Consent Decree. Submit within the 30-day window measured from the Federal Register publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address and routing for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should be addressed to the Assistant Attorney General, Environment and Natural Resources Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should refer to University of Minnesota v. United States, et. al., D.J. Ref. No. 90-11-3-11915. Mail: Assistant Attorney General, U.S. DOJ—ENRD, P.O. Box 7611, Washington, DC 20044-7611. Email: pubcomment-ees.enrd@usdoj.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted methods of submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments may be submitted either by email or by mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided email address (pubcomment-ees.enrd@usdoj.gov) or the provided postal address; follow any applicable formatting or content instructions in the notice (reference the case/D.J. reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference the case and DJ reference number
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should refer to University of Minnesota v. United States, et. al., D.J. Ref. No. 90-11-3-11915.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including the case caption and DOJ reference number ensures the comment is associated with the correct matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential public filing of comments (privacy/visibility warning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any comments submitted in writing may be filed by the United States in whole or in part on the public court docket without notice to the commenter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that written submissions might be placed on the public court docket; avoid including confidential or sensitive information if you do not want it publicly filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to access the proposed Consent Decree
rubrics_metrics.description: During the public comment period, the proposed Consent Decree may be examined and downloaded at this Justice Department website: https://www.justice.gov/enrd/consent-decrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the posted decree before commenting; the notice provides the DOJ webpage where the decree is available for inspection and download.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance for accessing the consent decree
rubrics_metrics.description: If you require assistance accessing the consent decree, you may request assistance by email or by mail to the addresses provided above for submitting comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact pubcomment-ees.enrd@usdoj.gov or the postal address if you need help obtaining or viewing the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use official Federal Register/PDF for legal research
rubrics_metrics.description: This site displays a prototype XML rendition and is not an official legal edition; verify results against an official edition of the Federal Register and use the PDF on govinfo.gov for the official electronic format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The XML rendition on FederalRegister.gov does not provide legal notice; for legal research or citation rely on the official SGML/PDF version on govinfo.gov and the official printed edition. Official editions provide legal notice under 44 U.S.C. 1503 & 1507.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document identification metadata to include or check
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice provides identifying information: agency (Department of Justice), document citation (89 FR 53644), document number (2024-14123), publication date (06/27/2024), and case caption (Regents of the University of Minnesota v. United States of America and E.I. DuPont De Nemours and Co., Case No. 17-cv-3690).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing or filing comments, confirm these identifiers to ensure correct docketing and context; include or reference appropriate citation details as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and subject-matter context
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed Consent Decree settles claims under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (42 U.S.C. 9607, 9613), the Minnesota Environmental Response and Liability Act (Minn. Stat. 115B.01, et seq.), and alleges breach of contract regarding environmental response actions and payment of response costs at the Gopher Ordnance Works Site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should be framed with awareness of the statutes and factual context at issue (CERCLA, state law, breach of contract claims) if addressing substantive legal or remedial issues.
